problem.user_text:
A packaging line runs a rotary cam-driven folding station at 420 cycles per minute, 20 hours a day. The flat-faced cam followers, 16 millimetres in diameter on fixed studs, develop surface fatigue spalls within 6 to 9 weeks of service, and metal debris from the spalling contaminates the food-contact belt, forcing line stops for cleaning roughly every 9 days. Lubrication is a once-per-shift manual grease gun routine that the crew already skips about one shift in five. The measured cam contact stress at the peak dwell is 1.4 gigapascals against a follower material rolling-contact limit near 1.7 gigapascals, but the measured oil film thickness ratio sits near 0.8, meaning asperity contact during every dwell. The line must keep 420 cycles per minute on the same cam mechanism, cannot change the cam profile (the camshaft is certified with the machine and re-cutting needs a six-week recertification), cannot switch to a different follower diameter class (the stud pattern is fixed), and cannot add any maintenance step the crew performs more than once per week.

evidence.title: Non-Linear Dynamic Analysis of a Cam With Flat-Faced Follower Linkage Mechanism
evidence.abstract: A mechanism with a cam and a flat-faced follower is considered for distinct angular velocities. The dynamic analysis presents follower linkage displacement driven by a cam rotating at a uniform angular velocity. The system has clearances between the flat-faced follower and the guides and the effect of clearance is analyzed. The cam-follower linkage mechanism is simulated using Solidworks program taking into account the impact and the friction between the cam, flat-faced follower, and the guides. The non-linear analysis tools are employed for the movement of the flat-faced follower. An experimental set up is established to capture the motion of the follower. High-resolution optical marker is mounted on the follower stem to capture the follower motion in the y-direction. The simulation and experimental results are compared and verified for largest Lyapunov exponent.</jats:p

evidence.title: Lubrication Analyses of Cam and Flat-Faced Follower
evidence.abstract: The principal factors that affect the characteristics of contact problem between cam and follower vary enormously during the operating cycle of this mechanism. This includes radius of curvature, surface velocities and applied load. It has been found over the last decades that the mechanism operates under an extremely thin film of lubricant. Any practical improvement in the level of film thickness that separates the contacted surfaces represents an essential step towards a satisfactory design of the system. In this paper a detailed numerical study is presented for the cam and follower (flat-faced) lubrication including the effect of introducing an axial modification (parabolic shape) of the cam depth on the levels of film thickness and pressure distribution. This is achieved based on a point contact model for a cam and flat-faced follower system. The results reveal that the cam form of modification has considerable consequences on the level of predicted film thickness and pressure distribution as well as surface deformation

evidence.title: A phase field model for hydrogen-assisted fatigue
evidence.abstract: We present a new theoretical and numerical phase field-based formulation for predicting hydrogen-assisted fatigue. The coupled deformation-diffusion-damage model presented enables predicting fatigue crack nucleation and growth for arbitrary loading patterns and specimen geometries. The role of hydrogen in increasing fatigue crack growth rates and decreasing the number of cycles to failure is investigated. Our numerical experiments enable mapping the three loading frequency regimes and naturally recover Paris law behaviour for various hydrogen concentrations. In addition, Virtual S-N curves are obtained for both notched and smooth samples, exhibiting a good agreement with experiments.

evidence.title: Microstructure sensitive fatigue life prediction model for SLM fabricated Hastelloy-X
evidence.abstract: A microstructure-sensitive fatigue life prediction framework based on CP-FFT is proposed to study SLM fabricated Hastelloy-X. The microstructure enters in the model through the shape, size and orientation distributions of grains in the RVEs, which are generated from experimental EBSD data. The framework has been applied to specimens built in two different directions with different polycrystalline microstructures and is able to accurately predict their fatigue life, using just two experiments for calibration. The model reproduces the better fatigue performance found experimentally at high stresses for samples built in transverse direction, identifying the origin of this anisotropy in grain aspect ratios.

evidence.title: DESIGN AND ANALYSIS OF CONSTANT-BREADTH CAM MECHANISM WITH OSCILLATING FLAT-FACED FOLLOWER
evidence.abstract: A simple yet comprehensive method is presented for the design and analysis of a constant-breadth cam mechanism with an oscillating flat-faced follower. In the proposed approach, the kinematic characteristics of the cam mechanism are first derived. The cam profile is then designed using homogenous coordinate transformation and conjugate surface theory. Moreover, the sliding velocity at the cam-follower contact points is determined. Finally, the pressure angle of the constant-breadth cam mechanism and the principal curvatures of the cam are analyzed. The validity of the proposed design methodology is verified by means of motion simulations performed using CAD software. </jats:p

evidence.title: A COMPUTERIZED APPROACH FOR TOLERANCE ANALYSIS OF DISK CAM MECHANISMS WITH A FLAT-FACED FOLLOWER
evidence.abstract: A computerized approach for analyzing the tolerances in disk cam mechanisms with a flat-faced follower is presented in this paper. Based on the simulated higher-pair contact analysis, the kinematic deviation of the follower motion caused by the tolerance amount of each design parameter can be determined numerically. The method is validated by means of analyzing the case of an eccentric circular cam mechanism; such a case has an exact solution of the follower motion error. Compared with the exact solutions, the presented computerized approach is demonstrated to be able to provide excellent accuracy and sufficient efficiency no matter how large the level of the tolerance is. Then, both the offset translating oblique flat-faced follower and the oscillating flat-faced follower cases are given to illustrate the presented method. The presented computerized approach and the obtained results can be helpful for tolerance allocation tasks of disk cam mechanisms with a flat-faced follower. </jats:p

mechanism_map.mechanism: The paper identifies clearance between the flat-faced follower and its guides as a source of impact and friction during follower motion, and shows that non-linear dynamic analysis (validated against experiment via the largest Lyapunov exponent) can quantify how this clearance-driven impact and friction governs follower motion — i.e., excessive guide clearance converts steady cam-driven displacement into impact-loaded, non-linear follower behavior that raises cyclic contact stress on the follower face, promoting surface fatigue spalling.
mechanism_map.intervention: Because the cam profile, 16 mm follower diameter, and 420 cycles/min are fixed, intervene on the guide-to-follower-stud clearance instead: build the paper's non-linear dynamic model of the folding-station cam-follower linkage (including clearance, impact, and friction), use it to identify the clearance value that minimizes impact severity, and re-specify the follower studs with close-fitting guide bushings/sleeves to hold that reduced clearance — with the certified cam geometry and follower diameter unchanged and no added maintenance beyond the weekly window.
mechanism_map.expected_effect: Lower impact and friction forces at the cam-follower interface reduce cyclic Hertzian contact stress on the 16 mm flat-faced follower, extending surface fatigue life well beyond the current 6–9 weeks and cutting the metal debris that contaminates the food-contact zone.
mechanism_map.falsification_test: Replicate the paper's optical-marker method on the running line: mount a high-resolution optical marker on a follower stem to capture y-direction motion at 420 cycles/min, extract the largest Lyapunov exponent and impact severity for the current clearance, then repeat with progressively reduced guide clearance; if reducing clearance does not measurably decrease impact severity/Lyapunov exponent and does not extend follower spalling life in a side-by-side trial, the mechanism is falsified.
mechanism_map.mechanism_source_span: The system has clearances between the flat-faced follower and the guides and the effect of clearance is analyzed.

cemetery_warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

custody_records.raw_content: A mechanism with a cam and a flat-faced follower is considered for distinct angular velocities. The dynamic analysis presents follower linkage displacement driven by a cam rotating at a uniform angular velocity. The system has clearances between the flat-faced follower and the guides and the effect of clearance is analyzed. The cam-follower linkage mechanism is simulated using Solidworks program taking into account the impact and the friction between the cam, flat-faced follower, and the guides. The non-linear analysis tools are employed for the movement of the flat-faced follower. An experimental set up is established to capture the motion of the follower. High-resolution optical marker is mounted on the follower stem to capture the follower motion in the y-direction. The simulation and experimental results are compared and verified for largest Lyapunov exponent.</jats:p

This is achieved based on a point contact model for a cam and flat-faced follower system. The coupled deformation-diffusion-damage model presented enables predicting fatigue crack nucleation and growth for arbitrary loading patterns and specimen geometries. The role of hydrogen in increasing fatigue crack growth rates and decreasing the number of cycles to failure is investigated. custody_records.raw_content: A microstructure-sensitive fatigue life prediction framework based on CP-FFT is proposed to study SLM fabricated Hastelloy-X. The microstructure enters in the model through the shape, size and orientation distributions of grains in the RVEs, which are generated from experimental EBSD data. The framework has been applied to specimens built in two different directions with different polycrystalline microstructures and is able to accurately predict their fatigue life, using just two experiments for calibration. The model reproduces the better fatigue performance found experimentally at high stresses for samples built in transverse direction, identifying the origin of this anisotropy in grain aspect ratios.

custody_records.raw_content: A simple yet comprehensive method is presented for the design and analysis of a constant-breadth cam mechanism with an oscillating flat-faced follower. In the proposed approach, the kinematic characteristics of the cam mechanism are first derived. The cam profile is then designed using homogenous coordinate transformation and conjugate surface theory. Moreover, the sliding velocity at the cam-follower contact points is determined. Finally, the pressure angle of the constant-breadth cam mechanism and the principal curvatures of the cam are analyzed. The validity of the proposed design methodology is verified by means of motion simulations performed using CAD software. </jats:p

custody_records.raw_content: A computerized approach for analyzing the tolerances in disk cam mechanisms with a flat-faced follower is presented in this paper. Based on the simulated higher-pair contact analysis, the kinematic deviation of the follower motion caused by the tolerance amount of each design parameter can be determined numerically. The method is validated by means of analyzing the case of an eccentric circular cam mechanism; such a case has an exact solution of the follower motion error. Compared with the exact solutions, the presented computerized approach is demonstrated to be able to provide excellent accuracy and sufficient efficiency no matter how large the level of the tolerance is. Then, both the offset translating oblique flat-faced follower and the oscillating flat-faced follower cases are given to illustrate the presented method. The presented computerized approach and the obtained results can be helpful for tolerance allocation tasks of disk cam mechanisms with a flat-faced follower. </jats:p
